sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Co-immunoprecipitation with Flag-CD300b: HA-CD300c successfully pulled down Flag-CD300b, demonstrating the tagged construct was expressed and retained its ability to form heteromeric complexes. Surface expression not directly measured by flow cytometry or equivalent.
sites.rationale: CD300C is a Type I single-pass transmembrane protein; its N-terminus (residues 21–183) is extracellular and its C-terminus (206–224) is intracellular, leaving exactly one extracellular terminus. The 'HA-CD300c' prefix notation in L1/L2 places the HA tag at the N-terminus; since no residue is named, the junction is topology-derived at insert_after_residue=20 (after signal peptide cleavage, P→G). Python confirms residue 20=P and residue 21=G. The insertion site is 163 residues from the TM boundary, well clear of the ≥3-residue constraint. Full-length HA-CD300c was expressed in COS-7 cells (which lack endogenous CD300 expression) and co-transfected with Flag-CD300b to study complex formation by co-immunoprecipitation. No residue number is stated in either L1 or L2; the 'HA-' prefix notation for this Type I TM protein places the tag at the extracellular N-terminus.

sources.claim: COS-7 cells, which lack endogenous CD300 expression, were co-transfected with HA-tagged CD300c and Flag-tagged CD300b in the wild type (wt) or mutant forms.

literature_notes: L1 and L2 are from the same paper (PMC5648872) and both describe the same HA-CD300c construct; L1 is used as the primary supporting clip because it describes the actual experimental use. L2 is a redundant methods citation for the same construct. No residue number is named in either clip, so position_evidence is topology_derived. The intracellular C-terminus (residues 206–224) does not qualify as a surface tag site. No internal loop insertions are reported in the ledger for CD300C.
